rules.name: Zero Plot Changes
rules.rule: Preserve plot, lore, reveals, outcomes, and established character identities.

rules.name: No Unauthorized Cutting
rules.rule: Do not remove established material simply to simplify a database entry.

rules.name: Continuity
rules.rule: Track time, locations, injuries, equipment, companions, knowledge, relationships, and cause-and-effect.

rules.name: Character Integrity
rules.rule: Preserve established motivations, personality, voice, history, relationships, and emotional continuity.

rules.name: Human Prose
rules.rule: Manuscript-facing material should feel authored, varied, emotionally grounded, and natural rather than mechanically generated.

rules.name: Repetition Control
rules.rule: Avoid overusing words, sentence structures, transitions, metaphors, and generic labels; replace only when context permits.

rules.name: Ledger Control
rules.rule: Do not overuse ledger when archive volume, book, record, folio, register, codex, document, or another established contextually correct term is more natural.

rules.name: D&D Integration
rules.rule: D&D races, creatures, terminology, magic concepts, and language categories may inform the framework, but Aethelgard-specific implementations remain original.

rules.name: Skull-Veil Identity
rules.rule: Skull-Veil is the nickname for the feared Elven faction. It is never the name of the sky-fissure creatures.

rules.name: Creature Separation
rules.rule: The hostile creatures from the violet fissure require a distinct species identity and terminology.

rules.name: Constructed Language
rules.rule: High Elven must have consistent grammar, phonology, vocabulary, register, romanization, and translation mappings.

rules.name: Language Variety
rules.rule: Do not repeatedly recycle a small set of roots or endings. Vocabulary must become genuinely large and structurally varied.

rules.name: Language Distinction
rules.rule: High Elven vocabulary should not sound like ordinary English/Common. Avoid accidental Common-looking words where a distinct form is possible.

rules.name: Language Frequency
rules.rule: Use High Elven substantially when Elven speakers naturally would, while preserving reader comprehension through context and selective translation.

rules.name: Lyra Fluency
rules.rule: Lyra learned High Elven through archival texts and treaties but did not grow up speaking it. Her spontaneous speech can show hesitation, uncertainty, and occasional self-correction.

rules.name: Native Fluency
rules.rule: Native Kael-Vossen speakers should use idiom, register, rhythm, and cultural assumptions naturally.

rules.name: Translator Compatibility
rules.rule: Every approved vocabulary item receives a stable meaning and translator mapping. Unknown forms are flagged rather than guessed.

rules.name: Contextual Translation
rules.rule: Do not translate every Elven sentence mechanically. Meaning may be communicated by action, response, and surrounding dialogue.

rules.name: Register
rules.rule: Maintain separate vocabulary and constructions for court, military, diplomatic, ritual, casual, and hostile speech.

rules.name: Abel's Bloodline
rules.rule: House Valerius carries historical responsibility in Kael-Vossen. Hatred and fear toward Abel and his companions must remain believable rather than disappearing immediately.

rules.name: Abel's Guilt
rules.rule: When confronted with the consequences of his family's actions, Abel's guilt should remain emotionally substantial while preserving his individual agency and established character.

rules.name: Elara's Fear
rules.rule: Threats to Abel can produce intense concern and panic in Elara when consistent with the scene, without erasing her established strength or agency.

rules.name: Development Labels
rules.rule: New material not established by the manuscript is marked development until deliberately canonized.

rules.name: No False Canon
rules.rule: Do not present invented details as established story facts without a canon or development marker.
